headline: Stocks tumble, erasing post-midterm gains as markets weigh future of AI build-out
author: Miriam Waldvogel

paragraphs.text: Major U.S. stock indexes tumbled Thursday, largely erasing post-election gains made the day before, as markets continued to absorb the broad impact of Democrats’ nationwide midterm success.
By market close on Thursday, the S&P 500, a broad index of 500 large American companies, had lost around 4 percent. The tech-heavy Nasdaq composite index was down around 5.5 percent.
Major tech stocks also took hits Thursday amid analyst concerns that the blue wave would snag America’s rapid AI build-out, with voters pushing back against data centers and the tech industry.

Dozens of ballot measures placing local restrictions on data center development were passed across the country Tuesday. States that have been hubs of data center development, including Texas and Ohio, will have new governors who have promised to regulate the projects more tightly.
Ira Jersey, chief U.S. interest rates strategist for Bloomberg Intelligence, said that could have consequences for the U.S. economy.
“With large states where people want to put a lot of data centers, if that pace of investment slows, that means the economy is going to slow somewhat,” he told Bloomberg Radio on Thursday.
“The market is getting a little bit worried and skeptical that the Fed is going to be able to continue to hike [interest rates], because maybe we’re going to have a slowdown,” Jersey said.
Investors sold off across the market, with shares of the bank JPMorgan Chase and manufacturer Caterpillar also down.

Companies linked to President Donald Trump and his political allies sold off more sharply than the broader markets. Elon Musk’s SpaceX, a major government contractor, was down around 9 percent Thursday afternoon. Trump Media & Technology Group, which operates the online platform Truth Social, was down around 10.5 percent.

Chip stocks took significant losses, with AI juggernaut Nvidia falling around 9 percent, enough to erase its year-to-date gains. Micron, a leading memory chip manufacturer, was down around 17.5 percent. Shares of Advanced Micro Devices, which reported strong earnings Tuesday, also fell around 17 percent.

Diane Swonk, chief economist at accounting firm KPMG, said on social media that she was considering the possibility that financial markets were experiencing either temporary wobbles or the start of a significant and long-lasting slump due to a bubble in expectations for AI.
“I hope our base case holds & that this is just another temporary setback,” she wrote. “Hope for the best but prepare for all outcomes.”
correctionA previous version of this article misstated the timing of the market drops. They occurred Thursday, not Wednesday.
